items.title: What Happens When a Master or Replica Fails
items.summary: A Master-Replica setup involves two nodes: Master and Replica. When a Replica crashes, it reconnects to the Master and resumes replication. If the Master crashes before propagating changes, Replica may lose data or cause conflicts. The first step is to identify the crashed Master. The process is similar for other nodes, including Replica. Master is the most critical component in a distributed data store, and its crash can result in business loss. A passive Master node is always in sync with the Master, making it a safe replacement. Once a new Master is set up, clients must be re-configured to send writes to the new Master. Writes during a Replica outage are handled by pulling updates through the proxy. In a Master-Replica setup, promoting an existing Replica as the new Master is the primary automation task.

items.summary: Hash join is a widely used join algorithm in distributed systems that combines with other algorithms like nested loop join to address specific problems in joining two tables across many nodes.

items.title: Leaderless Replication
items.summary: Leaderless replication is a fault-tolerant approach that eliminates the need for a single leader node, instead relying on quorum to ensure strong consistency across multiple nodes. This system can handle write operations even when a subset of nodes are down, making it a robust solution for multi-master setups.
